question: Does any other shortest, homologically trivial same-flux red-X correction loop pass the existing three-variable-site complete-second-law gate at the unchanged J7K physical error and first record?
role: Finite exact action-design feasibility screen; no joint charge law, expected risk, policy performance or noisy schedule sampling
source_basis: J7K homologically trivial six-edge loop and five-site censor
Lab 004 paper-normalized L=2 topology and ground-state-relative winding contract
J6L/J6M periodic geometry and anyon-free orbit
J7F frozen positive complete first record

model.geometry: Paper-normalized periodic L=2 honeycomb with 36 red edges; reconcile every red-edge ID and endpoints against J6L before using Lab 004 topology
model.fixed_physical_and_record: Private red-X physical edges [0,4,3], complete first public charge bits [1,1] at variable sites [1,2], mass 1/4, and the J7K anyon-free orbit; no post-screen record selection
model.public_actions: Baseline relation-free public correction [0]; each candidate is [0] symmetric-differenced with one simple, connected, nonbranching six-red-edge cycle. Future keys are unnecessary for this second-record feasibility screen; equal next flux follows from zero action-boundary difference and was checked for the J7K representative under fixed future keys.
model.hidden_boundary: Private physical support, orbit state and exact conditional marginals are scoring/generation internals; candidate red-X action edge sets and their flux are public. Token whitelistability is not actual frozen-JIT policy emission.
model.estimand: Count conditional nondeterministic eligible second-star sites per candidate under the same first record; pass only if count <=3. No complete joint second/next law and no action-effect magnitude is estimated.
model.independent_unit_uncertainty: Exhaustive deterministic finite-topology screen, no stochastic sample unit or uncertainty interval

matrix.cycle_enumeration: Enumerate every unique edge-set of simple six-edge cycles by deterministic vertex/edge DFS; deduplicate by sorted six-edge tuple and sort lexicographically. Classify every cycle with Lab 004 winding analysis. Screen every homologically trivial cycle, including the prior J7K cycle as a replay control; nontrivial cycles are excluded from admissible candidate actions and counted.
matrix.selection_rule: If one or more candidates pass, identify the lexicographically first passing sorted loop edge tuple solely as a prospective full-law candidate; do not calculate that law in this screen. Report every candidate and pass/fail count, including prior loop.
branches: all admissible equal-flux action/residual exact one-site second marginals
J7K cycle and baseline replay controls

competing_outcomes.one_or_more_pass: At least one homologically trivial six-edge same-flux candidate has <=3 variable second sites; a separately registered full-joint-law study may follow, without a policy or charge-benefit claim now
competing_outcomes.none_pass: No shortest trivial same-flux candidate meets the frozen cap on this fixed physical/first-record case; this does not rule out longer loops, other errors/records, or a newly justified larger exact-law budget
competing_outcomes.censored: Source/topology/replay/cycle-count/term/CPU/normalization gate fails; do not cherry-pick a subset or enlarge caps after observing output

acceptance: Seven pins pass before and after; all 36 red-edge IDs/endpoints reconcile
Every unique simple six-edge cycle is counted/classified with the exact Lab 004 homology rule and no unreported candidate exclusions
Each trivial cycle has zero public correction-boundary difference from baseline and exact conditional one-site marginals at every eligible second site; first-record mass is 1/4
J7K prior cycle replays five variable sites and baseline replays one; all per-candidate outcomes are retained
No joint charge law, risk score, policy-emission, noisy history, schedule arm, bootstrap, caller mutation or benefit claim
stop_rule: Fail closed on any pin, topology, enumeration, homology, replay, action-boundary, first-mass, eligibility, probability, CPU or term cap. Never select a subset after inspecting its marginals, increase the three-site cap, or promote one-site outcomes to a charge/risk law.
